candidate.attacker: A local process able to connect to the Chroma REST listener.
counterevidence: The per-request body buffer and parsed frame size are bounded.
HTTP.sys may impose entity-body timers; indefinite blocking of a single request is not established.
Static analysis establishes missing application-level limits, not a measured exhaustion threshold.
candidate.dataflow: Every accepted context is queued to the shared CLR thread pool without a concurrency gate. Each handler performs synchronous body reads before route dispatch and holds a thread-static 64 KiB buffer while waiting. Repeated incomplete request bodies accumulate outstanding work and occupy shared workers.

evidence.excerpt: ctx = l.GetContext(); ... ThreadPool.QueueUserWorkItem(static c => ... Handle(context), ctx);
body = _bodyBuf ??= new byte[64 * 1024]; ... req.InputStream.Read(body, bodyLen, body.Length - bodyLen)

candidate.impact: Resource pressure and starvation of unrelated thread-pool work in the elevated, long-running application.
candidate.invariant: Untrusted HTTP requests must have bounded simultaneous processing and body-read duration.
candidate.remediation: Enforce a bounded number of in-flight requests, reject excess requests, use asynchronous reads with a short explicit total-body deadline, and close/abort contexts in a finally block. Verify valid Chroma frames remain responsive while a bounded test set of clients sends incomplete bodies.
candidate.title: Chroma REST requests queue unbounded blocking body readers

deferred.reason: Application concurrency gap confirmed, but whole-app starvation/HTTP.sys effective limits require bounded runtime measurement.

candidate.attacker: A local process connecting to the GSI HTTP listener; no GSI token needed.
counterevidence: Bodies are size-bounded and GsiParser verifies the token.
HTTP.sys body timeouts may eventually release an individual blocked request.
Impact is confined to game-state integration; arbitrary code execution is not indicated.
candidate.dataflow: The sole accept loop calls Handle synchronously. Handle reads the complete body before parsing or authenticating it. An incomplete body blocks further GetContext calls, so legitimate game updates queue behind it.

evidence.excerpt: body = ReadBounded(reader); ... var parsed = GsiParser.Parse(body, Token); ... while ((n = reader.Read(buffer, 0, buffer.Length)) > 0)

candidate.impact: Game-state effects become stale/disconnected for the body-read timeout interval; repeated requests can sustain disruption.
candidate.invariant: An unauthenticated slow sender must not monopolize the only game-state processing thread.
candidate.remediation: Use bounded concurrent asynchronous handling with a short total-body deadline, guarantee response disposal on exceptions, and retain body-size/authentication checks. Verify legitimate token-bearing updates remain serviceable while another connection sends an incomplete body.
candidate.title: An incomplete unauthenticated GSI body blocks all game-state handling

deferred.reason: Serial pre-authentication body read confirmed; effective HTTP.sys timeout and game-silence impact need isolated Windows validation.

surfaces.notes: S3: embedded controls in names reach logs. Packet/client/time bounds already exist; intended LED control is not a finding. OpenRgbServer.cs:62,215,234,280.

surfaces.label: Baseline controls and source coverage
surfaces.notes:
Root/src/native security-policy resolver outputs were empty.
The app explicitly requires administrator privileges.
PawnIO installer verification pins an exact certificate RDN, obtains the signer from WinVerifyTrust state, and holds a no-write/no-delete sharing handle across verification and launches; the obvious temporary-file replacement attack is addressed.
Chroma named-pipe dimensions are bounded before allocation; ushort dimensions cannot wrap their product to a small positive int, so no integer-overflow allocation bypass was found.
Chroma pipe clients use SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION; a malicious pipe server cannot obtain an impersonation-capable token from the current shim.
OpenRGB packet allocations and controller counts have explicit caps; malformed managed parsing does not establish native memory corruption.
Native shim parameters are supplied by code already inside the hosting process; malformed pointers alone do not constitute a cross-boundary exploit.
Native shim full read found potential ordinary lifecycle/exception-handling concerns, but no validated additional security exploit.
No application execution, network access, exploit tests, or source modifications were performed.
Coverage focused on exposed listeners, updater, privileged executable loading and native shim; this is not a claim that every repository file was fully audited.
OpenRGB has a 16-client cap, 120-second per-read timeout, 3-second write timeout, and 1 MiB payload limit. No unbounded connection/thread allocation finding is warranted from this path.
OpenRGB ReadExactly uses per-read timeouts rather than a total packet deadline; slow progress can extend a packet lifetime. With intentional unauthenticated lighting control and bounded clients this is primarily optional hardening unless stronger availability requirements apply.
GSI stores at most approximately 512K decoded characters, despite the MaxBodyBytes name; it does not accept an unbounded body into memory. ContentLength64 is separately checked against 512 KiB.
No TimeoutManager, EntityBody, DrainEntityBody, or RequestQueue customization was found in src.
Chroma REST is started from MainViewModel alongside ChromaFeed and stopped during app shutdown.
Native shim opens the same named pipe and uses overlapped writes with a 50 ms wait plus cancellation. Only relevant pipe I/O sections were inspected, not the full native file.
The pipe DACL intentionally retains GENERIC_WRITE compatibility for installed shims; do not present the documented compatibility decision alone as an undiscovered exploit.
HTTP.sys effective timeout defaults were not verified because this task prohibited network and application execution.

surfaces.label: Architecture consumer reconciliation
surfaces.notes:
Chroma pipe and REST ingestion are unconditional normal GUI startup surfaces, not only active-effect initialization (src/UnifiedRgb.App/MainViewModel.cs:1239).
GUI OpenRGB SDK server is distinct from the managed OpenRGB bridge process. Do not transfer GUI loopback-binding guarantees to the external child without inspecting the external server's effective configuration.
SDK ingress already caps connection count, packet size, and socket timeouts; claims of unrestricted payload allocation must account for those controls (src/UnifiedRgb.Core/Net/OpenRgbServer.cs:62; src/UnifiedRgb.Core/Net/OpenRgbServer.cs:215; src/UnifiedRgb.Core/Net/OpenRgbServer.cs:234).
Public update checks do occur via GitHub despite stale Backend comments saying they skip (src/UnifiedRgb.Core/AppPaths.cs:32; src/UnifiedRgb.Core/UpdateClient.cs:43).
AppPaths separates roaming/local state but does not itself apply privileged ACLs (src/UnifiedRgb.Core/AppPaths.cs:27).
Update payload/script staging is beside the actual process executable, not TEMP; any staging concern must use that complete location (src/UnifiedRgb.App/Services/UpdateService.cs:109).
Actual installation ACLs and external OpenRGB server binding/dependency internals remain deployment questions.
